name: Boundless Way Zen Temple
technique: Zazen (shikantaza and koan introspection) within a formal sesshin schedule
influences: Korean Linji lineage of Seung Sahn (via Zen Master George Bowman)
teacherAccess: Daily dokusan (private teacher interviews) during sesshin, led in person by resident transmitted teachers including Melissa Blacker Roshi and David Rynick Roshi.
retreatOptions: 2-day outdoor retreats, 3-day and 7-day residential sesshin, and a 7-14 day Summer Residency program (weeks can be combined for up to 3 weeks).
about: Boundless Way Zen Temple (Mugendo-ji) is a Zen Buddhist temple in Worcester, Massachusetts, offering residential training in a Soto/Rinzai-influenced lineage founded by James Ford, Melissa Blacker, and David Rynick. The temple hosts several week-long residential sesshin each year, an annual multi-week Summer Residency leading into Summer Sesshin, and shorter outdoor practice retreats offsite. Residential days combine zazen, kinhin, teisho (dharma talks), dokusan, samu (work practice), and formal oryoki-style meals, largely in silence. The community also runs extensive weekly and online practice, but its core intensive offerings are on-site, multi-day residential retreats at the Worcester temple.
schedule: Roughly six residential week-long sesshin plus jukai ceremonies annually, a 7-14 day Summer Residency in July-August, and 2-day outdoor retreats each spring and fall, alongside daily/weekly practice.
cost: Suggested-donation registration fees scaled by retreat length and membership status, with pay-what-you-can accommodation if the suggested fee is a barrier.

pricePerDay.notes: Derived from suggested residential sesshin registration fees: 7-day $750 (member) to $840 (non-member) and 3-day $325 (member) to $360 (non-member), divided by nights.

foodNotes: Meals are lacto-vegetarian and served formally (oryoki-style during sesshin); allergies and dietary needs accommodated on request.
workNotes: Daily samu (work practice) and meal cleanup are built into the residential sesshin schedule.
